title: Devlog: what was really capping the lane count
summary: The kernel, not the lanes, holds the memory that limits how many lanes can run.
changes: With the target at 52 the supervisor stalled at about 14 lanes. The system's counters show 14.5 GB in the kernel's non-paged pool after 2.5 days without a restart, against a normal figure well under 2 GB; the 14 lanes themselves use about 2 GB.
The health check now reports that pool and logs each reading so its growth can be measured. Only a restart of the machine returns the memory, which is the owner's decision.

title: Devlog: hourly review, 18:08
summary: The sixth hourly review, written as the swarm was parked.
changes: 10,873 functions verified, 16.0% of the code by size. The model quota ran out at 17:42 and every lane stopped; the cloud review was merged and checker version 5 put live while nothing was running.
The step that hands back stopped lanes' work was rewritten and released 948 functions; the production brief is version b9.

title: Devlog: merging the cloud review, and three traps on the way to checker version 5
summary: What was checked before the merge, what went wrong while checking, and what was decided.
changes: Records that checker version 5 reproduces every verdict on record on this machine, and that one of its options cannot work here because the system holds the address range it needs in every 32-bit process.

Records three traps: a build that was not rebuilt because unpacked sources carried old times, a merge plan that would have changed the checker under running lanes, and a supervisor that kept starting lanes after the model quota ran out.
Records why the step that hands back stopped lanes' work had released almost nothing, and its first real run: 948 functions from 68 lanes.

title: Checker: version 5 is the live checker
summary: The worker built from the merged source replaced version 4 while no lane was running.
changes: Version 5 was built from main after the merge and run through the whole regression with the live driver: all 38 existing proofs and all 34 wrong versions give the verdicts on record, and the five new proofs that can run on this machine pass with their wrong versions caught. The version 4 worker and proof library are kept beside the new ones.
The scripts that rank checker versions and the schema for lane results now know version 5, so a pass under it is recorded as such and counts as verified.

The production brief is version b9: it tells lanes what version 5 adds (x87 entry values, vector arguments beyond the second, larger snapshots) and that the read-only shadow option cannot work on this machine, with the deferral reason to use.

The step that hands back the work of stopped lanes was rewritten. It released a batch only when the lane had left no results file at all; many stopped lanes had one written by the checker driver itself, so their batches stayed reserved for good. It now keeps what a lane settled and what is already in the verified tree, and released 948 functions from 68 stopped lanes.

title: Site: the tick regenerates the progress history, quality data and devlog feed
summary: Three pages that arrived with pull request 1 read data files that nothing was refreshing.
changes: The status script now runs the three site generators after it writes the progress file: the series behind the progress chart, the numbers behind the quality page, and the devlog's Atom feed. Their output is committed with the progress commit every five minutes.

Each generator was run by hand first: together they take about fifteen seconds, and each writes only when its output changed. If one fails, its file is left as it was, the failure is printed, and the tick carries on.

title: Changelog: the commits of pull request 1
summary: One entry for each commit the cloud review brought, and one for the merge.
changes: Every commit has a changelog entry whose title is its subject. The 85 commits merged as pull request 1 were written in a cloud session that could not edit the changelog without conflicting with the five-minute tick, so their entries are added here, taken from each commit's own message.
The merge's entry records how the branch was checked before merging and what does not work on the coordinator's machine.

title: Merge pull request 1: the cloud review
summary: A cloud session reviewed the repository without the game's files; its 85 commits are merged, each with its own entry below.
changes: Before merging, the branch's checker (version 5) was built and run on the coordinator's machine against the game's executable: all 38 existing proofs and all 34 wrong versions give the verdicts on record, and the new proofs for x87 entry values, vector arguments beyond the second and large snapshots pass with their wrong versions caught.

One new checker option cannot work on this machine: the read-only shadow of the original's preferred address range. In every 32-bit process here the system already holds that range, so the worker cannot place the shadow there. Functions that need it stay deferred on this machine.

The first local run of that regression was wrong and is discarded: sources unpacked from an archive carry the commit's time, so the build tool judged an older proof library current and did not rebuild it. The library was rebuilt from clean and the regression run again.
Merged while no lane was running (the model subscription's quota had run out), so no lane had the checker changed underneath it.

The live five-minute tick still runs the coordinator's own copies of the operating scripts. Its structure count now reads every source file of the types crate, which this merge splits into one module per subsystem; the count is unchanged at 340.
Two fact labels are renamed in the tracked copy of the counting script to say what they count; they take effect when the tick switches to the tracked scripts.

summary: From the cloud review merged as pull request 1.

Also fixed: --out with a bare file name crashed, and ledger.load_game_set left its file open.

Not installed anywhere by this commit.

title: CI: the publication check can check given files or the staged content

title: Lints: digit separators, and exact float comparisons allowed in parser tests

title: Lints: machine-applicable clippy fixes across the portable crates
summary: From the cloud review merged as pull request 1.

title: Formatting: cargo fmt across the workspace
summary: From the cloud review merged as pull request 1.

title: Shader translator: a listing, a SPIR-V text dump and a coverage census for debugging translations
summary: From the cloud review merged as pull request 1.
changes: Three debugging aids. A listing of decoded programs, one line per instruction with the dword offset translation errors report, registers, masks, swizzles, modifiers, declarations and exact constants. A readable dump of the emitted SPIR-V that names every opcode the crate emits and flags anything it cannot account for, round-trip tested over every test module. A census that reports, per program, whether it translates, what stops it, and which opcodes, register files and modifiers are used, so a run over a player's own shaders shows what fraction translates. Output from the game's shaders is a disassembly of game code: the docs say it stays on the user's machine and is never committed. Tests go from 113 to 142.

title: Tools: lf-lift-diff runs both sides of a slot-table case against one test buffer

changes: The first 32-bit run on the Windows runner failed three of 47 cases: the verified rewrite and the lift ran against two buffers, so every address either side computed differed by the distance between them while results, regions and the whole image agreed. The host stand-in's relocation now depends on the installed buffer, as the real runtime's does, so the host reproduces this kind of mistake (it reproduced the CI failure, first failing input included). The lift itself was right and is unchanged; its docs and the method document record the run and its cause.

title: Checker worker: x87 entry values, XMM2-7 call arguments, wide snapshots and the preferred-base window

Changed defaults, stricter than before: the worker is linked at a fixed high base and reserves the original's preferred-base window, so an unrelocated absolute read by the original faults with an abs-window note instead of silently reading worker memory (the cause of the read-only constant misread in devlog production-b145; an opt-in read-only shadow serves such reads where a contract needs them); the FPU is reset after each side; an unknown snapshot kind is an error. title: Shaders: lf-dxso-spirv translates shader model 3.0 bytecode to SPIR-V for Vulkan
summary: From the cloud review merged as pull request 1.
changes: The game's shaders are precompiled Direct3D 9 shader model 3.0 programs (969 distinct ones). A local lane already proved that external tools can translate them all, but that output is game-derived and can never be committed; this crate does the translation inside the project, on each player's own copy, with no dependencies and no unsafe. It decodes every model 3 instruction and register file, translates arithmetic, flow control, loops with relative addressing, subroutines, predication and texture sampling to SPIR-V 1.0, and returns the reflection a renderer needs. The Vulkan binding convention (uniform buffers per stage, combined image samplers, vertex input and varying locations by usage, the half-pixel and clip-space fixups) lives in one module. Anything unsupported returns an error instead of wrong code; every Direct3D 9 semantic choice that is a guess is labelled Inferred. 113 tests, including a structural SPIR-V validator and a small interpreter that executes translated programs. Requested by the owner ahead of the renderer phase.

title: Agent rules: what the first 800 lanes taught, written down for the next wave
summary: The lessons of the first day and a half of production are now in the rules every lane reads, and in the production brief.
changes: Rule 3 gains four requirements: a pass counts only on the stock checker; every function gets its own deliberately wrong version, which must fail; a proof says what it does not cover; floating-point results match bit for bit, and a difference is fixed in the rewrite.

The working rules for lanes gain nine lessons, each with the incident behind it: read the clock; write results early and keep them current; triage a batch for what cannot be tested before spending the hour; read the executable through its mapped image; generate families of near-identical functions; follow the best lane's output as the standard; leave no process running; never build anything large in one piece; lists for programs are data files.
A table says where a lane's Rust goes on every five-minute tick: verified rewrites, unverified rewrites, and other lanes' code waiting for review.

The models section records what was measured: maximum reasoning effort is faster and verifies more than the next setting down; batches of 40 small functions and generator lanes for families are kept; six checker workers and one-function lanes are dropped; the second model is on hold and its habits were written into the brief.

The production brief is version b8: batches of 40, and three working rules added (leave nothing running, triage for untestable batches, results first). The tracked copy of the brief notes carries the same version.

title: Devlog: entries move into a SQLite database, searched in the browser
summary: The devlog page had grown to 1.5 MB of HTML with 315 entries. The entries are now rows in a database that the page downloads once and queries locally, as a blog with search.

The devlog page is now a small shell. It opens the database in the browser and lists the posts newest first, 30 at a time, with a topic filter. Selecting a post shows it on its own with links to the newer and older ones. Nothing is queried on a server.

Two ways to search. Exact: one SQL query in which every word must appear and words in quotes must appear together. Close: ranks posts by how well each word matches the words a post uses, allowing near spellings and word beginnings, and says what each word was matched as. The search and the topic are kept in the address, so a search can be shared as a link.

Entries are added with scripts/devlog_db.py, and lane fragments still go through the same publication checks before they are written. The status script counts entries from the database. The agent rules describe the new way to add and change an entry.

The database reader is the sql.js library, loaded from a public content network with an integrity hash so that a changed file is refused. Topics are derived from each entry's id and title; no lane has to tag anything.

title: Tooling: the operating scripts are in the repository
summary: The scripts that run the lane swarm lived in an untracked scratch folder. Cleaned copies are now tracked and tested.
changes: scripts/coordinator/ holds the 16 live scripts of the operating layer (the five-minute tick, the lane launcher and supervisor, the brief makers, the importer of passed rewrites, the count, review and report scripts), four shared modules, and tests. Lessons from today's incidents are built in: lanes are started so that they outlive their launcher, the supervisor reads its settings on every pass, a dead lane's batch is released but never within fifteen minutes of its launch.

These copies are not yet the ones in use. The lane could not run anything that commits, pushes or starts lanes, so the tick, the supervisor and the importers were ported line by line and need a supervised first run before the scratch copies are retired.

title: CI: a first pipeline on GitHub Actions
summary: Every push that touches code is now built and tested on GitHub's machines. It informs; nothing waits on it.
changes: Portable crates (engine crates, format readers, shared types) are built and their tests run on Windows, Linux and macOS. The goal is a portable game, so portability is checked from the first day instead of at the end.
The 32-bit Windows tools (the checker's worker and runtime, the proof library, the loader's hook engine, replacement table and proxy) are built, and their unit tests run.

A publication check runs on every push: nothing from the game or the scratch folders is tracked, no binary or game file types, no machine paths or account names in text files, no inline assembly in rewrites or engine crates, no file over 5 MB. The repository passes it today (7,318 tracked files).
Formatting and lints run as advisory: findings are reported and never turn a run red until the code is clean under both.

Runs are triggered only by changes to code, scripts or the workflow, so the progress, devlog and rewrite-import commits that arrive every few minutes do not start one. A newer push cancels an older run.

What it cannot do: run the checker against the original game. That needs the game's executable, which is never uploaded anywhere. The rewrites under rewrites/pending are not compiled here yet either; they join when the assembly step lands.

title: Checker version 4: lane fixes folded back, two silent passes closed
summary: The tracked checker gains the harness abilities lanes had built in private copies, and fails loudly in two cases where it used to pass without comparing.
changes: A stand-in for a called function can now leave registers as it found them, for originals that rely on the real callee doing so (a base constructor that keeps the object pointer; a check called after the return value is set). Without this, a run of 80 constructors could not be verified at all.

New contract options, all off by default so version 3 contracts run unchanged: an argument passed in the accumulator, a callee that leaves stack clean-up to its caller, an out-parameter written at an offset, and a byte mask on a pushed argument for one-byte values pushed as full words. A mask is recorded in the verdict and a mask of zero is rejected.

Closed: when one trial made more calls than the call log holds, the calls past the limit were not compared and the verdict was still a pass. That now fails, and a contract can raise the limit to 1,024.

Closed: asking for the accumulator to be compared at a call without the option that carries it compared zeros on both sides. That now fails. The coordinator's review added the reverse rule: using the option without asking for the comparison also fails, because the argument would be compared nowhere.
A trial lost because the worker died or timed out is retried on a fresh worker, at most twice, and every retry is recorded in the verdict. Lanes had been doing this by hand.

When the only difference in a failing trial is the sign or payload of a not-a-number, the verdict says so and points at operand order. The trial still fails. The proposal to treat such values as equal was not taken.

Regression on the rebuilt worker: all 38 proofs and all 34 deliberately wrong versions give the same result as before. Not done in this version: arguments on the x87 stack and vector-register arguments beyond the second.

title: Checker worker: call log no longer overruns at 256 calls
summary: A one-opcode fix that three production lanes independently traced to the same line.

title: Checker version 3: closing the ways a wrong rewrite could pass
summary: Fixes for the defects and gaps that lanes using checker version 2 reported, each proven on the functions that exposed it.
changes: Random fills for global data now vary per word and per trial; the old generator was nearly constant, which weakened every test of a function that reads globals.

Call arguments are logged and compared up to 40 words instead of 8, and the stack is cleaned correctly after calls with many arguments. A rewrite with two later arguments swapped used to pass and now fails.
Random inputs no longer point into the original's code, which had made faithful rewrites look like cheats; the detection of rewrites that read or call the original is unchanged.

Callees can be scripted with a sequence of answers (for loops that poll until done), tail jumps that forward stack arguments are handled, and the input forms that stopped some earlier contracts being ported are supported.

title: Engine page: revised after an independent design review
summary: A critic agent scored the first version 6 out of 10; this change fixes the problems it ranked highest.
changes: The line map now defines frame and thread in one sentence, shows each line's measured thread count, draws the hand-off of the draw list from the game thread to the render thread, and has a marker riding each rail to show the lines run at once.
Stop details moved to a fixed panel beside the map so pressing a stop no longer moves the page; each stop now says what was measured and what is inferred, and a Next stop button walks through all 21.
On narrow screens the four lines collapse and open one at a time, with details opening under the pressed stop.
The unreadable-megabyte strip was drawn at about 25% of the width for a 9% share; it is now drawn in true proportion with its labels in a key.

The frame-rate ruler now labels its ticks, shades the part of a frame after the last whole millisecond, offers 30, 60, 144 and 240 presets, and states the error as up to 1 ms instead of claiming exact readings at round frame times.

The task diagram became three layers with an event arrow into each, the function chart's title and note now say it counts functions and not bytes, causal claims that were not measured were reworded, and key numbers are set large.

title: Record the encrypted code range
summary: A correction: about 9% of the code section is encrypted on disk.

Devlog: Ghidra refuses project folders under a path element starting with a dot, so the project is addressed through a junction with a dot-free path.
Plan: the encrypted range is opaque to every tool and excluded from counts. The project does not decrypt it or dump it from a running process.

AGENTS.md gains rule 6: never add, link to or describe how to obtain game files, keys, cracks or ways around copy protection, and never design for a pirated copy.

title: Add the devlog
summary: Research notes and lessons, so nobody has to rediscover them.
changes: Sixteen entries covering a first look at the executable's headers, what the first estimates got wrong, why the route is direct to Rust, harness design from other projects, replacing functions in the running game, what is known about the executable, the Xbox 360 recompilation projects and what went wrong for them, tools, dependencies, frame-rate coupling, working with agent lanes, building the site, precedents, upscalers and open questions.
Every finding is labelled Verified, Inferred or Unknown and linked to its source.

title: Add the changelog page
summary: This page.
changes: Lists every commit, newest first, from docs/data/changelog.json.

title: Add the project site overview
summary: The front page of the GitHub Pages site in docs.
changes: A map of the executable's code from start to end, where each square changes shade as its functions are identified, named, rewritten and verified. With no data it shows a plain statement that nothing is measured yet.
Progress meters, the method step by step, the repository rule, the roadmap, the planned features and platforms, and credits.
Six placeholder concept images, generated for the page and captioned as not being screenshots.
Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step. Works at phone, tablet and desktop widths, in light and dark themes, and the map can be read with the keyboard.

title: Add progress tracking
summary: One data file drives the badges and the site's numbers.
changes: docs/data/progress.json holds the counts: phase, functions, stages, structures, symbols and the code map. Everything is zero or empty because nothing has been measured.
scripts/update_progress.py regenerates the seven SVG badges and the site's data files from it, and fills commit hashes into the changelog.
The badges are generated into the repository, so they need no external badge service.

title: Add the project plan
summary: plan.md: the goal, the decisions and why, and the eight phases.
changes: Goal and target platforms: Windows x64, Windows on ARM and macOS, with upscaling, frame generation and path tracing as later work.
Decisions: rewrite straight to Rust with no committed C++ stage, check each function by emulator comparison, then swap it into the running game behind a switch.
Eight phases with exit gates, and the phase 0 task list.
Harness design taken from other projects, the dependency table, pitfalls from the recompilation projects' history, risks and open questions.
First findings from the executable's headers: built with Visual Studio 2012, link-time code generation in use, main code not encrypted, class names present.

title: Add the agent rules
summary: AGENTS.md: what every agent and contributor must follow.
changes: Rule 1: no decompiled code in any tracked file. Only structures, symbols and Rust rewrites derived from the game may be committed.
Rule 2: publishing is the owner's decision; agents never push or post.
Rule 3: a machine check decides when a function is done, and fake passes are banned.
Rule 4: the coordinator keeps the progress file true, from machine sources only.
Rule 5: anything private goes in the untracked notes file and nowhere else.
Commit history is one change per commit, each with a changelog entry; lessons go in the devlog.

title: Add the repository layout
summary: Where things live, and what git never sees.
changes: Everything generated (build output, caches, logs, agent scratch work, decompiler output) goes under .artifacts, which git ignores.
The local toolchain (tools, .venv), the original executable (orig) and the private notes file are ignored too.
Game files, Ghidra and IDA databases and stray build output are blocked by extension wherever they land.
Cargo builds are redirected into .artifacts so no target folder appears in the tree.
Line endings are LF, with CRLF only for .bat, .cmd and .ps1.
